newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: New black SAfrica leisure group plans fun centre.
newsitem.headline: New black SAfrica leisure group plans fun centre.

text.p: Black empowerment group MoAfrika Casino Holdings (Pty) Ltd on Wednesday unveiled plans for a 2.5 billion rand retail and leisure centre it plans to build within the next three years.

The group, which has formed a consortium with 10 black empowerment companies and Ladbroke Group Plc's local subsidiary, Ladbroke Casino Holdings, said the centre would be the first of its kind in South Africa.
MoAfrika's chairman Rufus Maruma said the centre would contain retail outlets and entertainment facilities, while being augmented by a luxury hotel, a golf course and a casino complex.
To this end, it had submitted a bid for one of Gauteng province's six casino licences.

The whole of MoAfrika's investment establishment had the potential to generate directly and indirectly 7,000 permanent and 15,000 temporary jobs, primarily for the people living in the black settlements of Tembisa and Ivory Park near the proposed site of the centre in Midrand, north-east of Johannesburg, Maruma said.

"A key focus of MoAfrka is the development of affirmative business enterprises," Maruma said in a statement, adding the consortium's goals included setting up a hotel school and a retail academy to train black traders in the area.
A 145-room luxury hotel, near the centre, would be built by the Ladbroke Group through its Hilton International hotels division and expansion plans allowed for a further 120 rooms, Maruma said.
It was planned that the hotel will employ about 120 people.
David Attenborough, Africa development director for Ladbroke Casinos said: "We are proposing a casino with 2,000 slot machines and 100 gaming tables."
Also built into the plans of the centre is a water theme park which will be intergrated into the centre, Marumo said.
Marumo said the U.S.-based NBSG, the designers of Disney's Waterworld, had been taken aboard to help in its development.
"MoAfrika will therefore be a cultural centre for Gauteng and will become one of the province's premier tourists destinations," Marumo added.
